_about: Field terms for F310, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

titius-bode.definition: any formula that places a system's planets at distances or periods growing by a near-constant ratio from one planet to the next, here fitted in three forms to the log of orbital period
titius-bode.excludes: a physical model of how planets form or migrate

peas-in-a-pod.definition: the pattern, reported from Kepler data, that planets inside one system tend to be alike in size and in the ratios between neighbouring periods
peas-in-a-pod.excludes: a rule for the order of the gaps, and any likeness between planets of different systems

leave-one-out.definition: dropping one interior planet, fitting the rule to the others and comparing the predicted period with the true one, repeated for every interior planet
leave-one-out.excludes: scoring a planet with a fit that has already seen it

sha-256.definition: a hash function that turns a file into a 64-character fingerprint which changes if any byte of the file changes; a recorded hash shows the file was not edited after it was taken
sha-256.excludes: encryption, because the hash keeps nothing secret and cannot be turned back into the file

order-shuffle.definition: each system rebuilt from its own innermost period and its own gaps in log period, put in a random order, and scored with the same form and freedom as the real system
order-shuffle.excludes: gaps borrowed from other systems, which the pooled-gap control uses

pooled-gap.definition: each system rebuilt from gaps in log period drawn at random from all systems' gaps, and scored with the same form and freedom as the real system
pooled-gap.excludes: planets or gaps from outside the 122 systems in the sample

law-like.field: our usage, fixed in the preregistration
law-like.definition: the verdict that a Titius-Bode form beats the order-shuffle control's 95th percentile and predicts dropped planets better than the neighbour baseline
law-like.excludes: regularity that similar gaps alone produce, which beats only the pooled-gap control

tap.definition: the Table Access Protocol of the International Virtual Observatory Alliance, the standard query interface through which astronomical archives return table rows
tap.excludes: any selection or cleaning of the rows, which the query itself sets

controversy-flag.definition: a catalogue field set to 1 when a planet's existence or confirmation has been questioned in the published literature and 0 otherwise
controversy-flag.excludes: independent confirmation, which a flag of 0 does not give

transit.definition: a search that finds planets by the small dip in a star's light as a planet crosses its disc, which favours short periods and orbits seen close to edge-on
transit.excludes: planets found only by other methods, such as radial velocity or direct imaging

rms-residual.definition: the square root of the mean squared difference between fitted and observed log period across a system's planets, a measure of scatter about the fit
rms-residual.excludes: any offset or trend the fit has already absorbed into its parameters

geometric-mean.definition: for two numbers, the square root of their product, which is the plain average taken on a log scale; here the neighbour baseline for a dropped planet's period
geometric-mean.excludes: the ordinary average of the two periods, which is larger whenever they differ
